messages:
alex.g: Quick design check — noticed when action cards collapse on narrow dashboard, the skeleton loader covers the primary CTA and keyboard focus lands under it. Also seeing the toast slide-up overlap the collapsed card on mobile. Screenshot + short vid attached. :grimacing:

maya.k: Ugh yeah saw that in staging. Repro steps? is it only when list-height < 120px?

alex.g: Steps: shrink window to ~320px, trigger collapse, click the row to load details (we show skeleton). Primary CTA moves into overflow (kebab) and focus ends up on the hidden button. Toast for "Saved" uses bottom anchor and sits over the card.

samuel: Likely layering + DOM order. Skeleton is absolutely positioned on top of the card content. When we move CTA into overflow we probably don't update tabindex. Quick thought — set the skeleton to pointer-events: none; and toggle aria-hidden on content elements when skeleton is visible.

jordan: Also consider whether the CTA should move into header instead of kebab on collapse. That reduces focus juggling. Would need spacing token tweaks for header density. cc @maya.k

luca: From an a11y POV: if something visually moves to overflow, keyboard focus must be redirected. We shouldn't let focus remain on an invisible element. Use `element.focus()` to land on the first visible actionable item, and set `aria-hidden="true"` on the hidden actions. Also add `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` for the toast so screen readers announce it without stealing focus.

maya.k: Agree with header CTA. Visually, header CTA keeps affordance consistent across breakpoints. We can reduce button padding by the compact spacing token (`space-2` -> `space-1`) to make it fit. Thoughts on visual hierarchy if header gets a primary CTA?

alex.g: Hierarchy ok — header CTA would be the same visual weight as desktop primary, but on collapsed rows it becomes the single action. We should probably switch to a ghost style on mobile to avoid dominance.

samuel: Implementation notes:
```css
.card-skeleton { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; }
.card-content[aria-hidden="true"] { visibility: hidden; }
:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); border-radius: 6px; }
```
That avoids blocking clicks and keeps focus ring visible when we programmatically focus header CTA.

jordan: Toast overlap — can we change toast anchor from bottom to `bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` + use `translateY(8px)` when there's a collapsed card? Or use toast stacking rules: if a component with `data-overlay` is present, toast uses top anchor. Might be simpler: detect collapsed mode and position toast above the cards container.

luca: Just make sure whichever position we choose, the toast is announced with `role=status` but not `alert` to avoid interrupting. Keep `aria-atomic=false` unless we need full read.

maya.k: Copy nit: current toast says "Saved" — for clarity in this context use "Card updated" or "Changes saved to card" depending on action. Short but scannable. Also CTA label in header should be something like "Open" vs "View details"? I prefer verbs that match the immediate action — "Open" is ambiguous. Maybe "View" or "Edit" depending on state.

alex.g: Good call. I'll test "View details" at 10 chars. If header CTA gets cramped, we can use an icon + visually hidden label for screen readers.

samuel: Dev checklist I can pick up: (1) add aria-hidden toggle, (2) pointer-events fix for skeleton, (3) programmatic focus on visible CTA, (4) toast repositioning logic behind a feature flag.

alex.g: Perfect. Can you spin up a quick branch and drop a PR link here? I'll mock the copy and create a small visual diff in Figma for header CTA + reduced padding token.

samuel: Will do — assigning to eng-frontend. PR when ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web/pull/4152 (WIP) :hammer_and_wrench:

jordan: Quick design acceptance criteria idea: 1) keyboard tab sequence lands on header CTA after collapse, 2) toast does not overlap card content, 3) focus ring is visible against skeleton overlay, 4) mobile density respects `space-1` token.

luca: I'll run a quick screen reader pass after PR lands. Also verify voiceover / talkback announcements for toast text.

alex.g: Thanks all. I'll update the Figma and add the copy options: "Card updated" / "Changes saved" / "Saved" and link it in the PR. Marking as in-progress. :thumbsup:
